title: A Port tenant gave $75,000 at the Mayor’s request, 232 days after its lease was approved

beats.text: 29 July 2025: the City approves a Pier 9 lease for Autodesk.
232 days later…
Autodesk gives 75,000 dollars to a committee carrying the Mayor’s name. At his request.

visual.label: to a committee carrying the Mayor’s name, 18 March 2026

beats.text: This is a lead, not a finding.

visual.line: This is a lead, not a finding: a pattern in public records. This film says what the records show, what they do not show, and what would settle it.

beats.text: Autodesk rents space at Pier 9 from the Port.

visual.text: Real Property Lease - Retroactive - Autodesk Inc. - Pier 9 - Monthly Rent $147,018.12

beats.text: The Board approved the lease 11 to 0, retroactively. Its term began in February 2025.
The Port gave procedural delays and staff turnover as the reason it came late.
Two notices list Autodesk as a City contractor: the Board’s, and the Mayor’s.

visual.text: the Board’s, signed 4 August 2025 · the Mayor’s, signed 22 August 2025

beats.text: City agreements bar a contractor’s gifts to a committee the approving official controls.

visual.line: Section 1.126: “a committee controlled by such elected official or a candidate for that office”

beats.text: For twelve months after approval. And leases of land or buildings are named.

visual.label: months after the City approves the contract
visual.sub: leases “of any land or building” are named

beats.text: On 18 March 2026, Autodesk gave 75,000 dollars to the Daniel Lurie Ballot Measure Committee.

visual.text: Daniel Lurie Ballot Measure Committee - Safe, Affordable MUNI for a Thriving San Francisco · $75,000 · 2026-03-18

beats.text: Its statement of organization, Form 410,

visual.text: Controlled committee · Daniel Lurie, Mayor · controlling officeholder

beats.text: names Mayor Lurie as its controlling officeholder.

visual.text: Controlled committee · Daniel Lurie, Mayor · controlling officeholder

beats.text: Count from either approval date: 232 days, or 225. Both inside twelve months.
The Mayor’s own Form 114.5 reports that money as given at his request.

visual.text: Autodesk · $75,000 · made at the request of Mayor Daniel Lurie

beats.text: A State rule limits asking a party for money, for 12 months after a decision.

visual.line: “for 12 months after the agency renders a final decision on the matter”

beats.text: How rare is this? From 2017 to 2026, the filings show it 6 times.

visual.label: contributions, 2017 to 2026, from a contractor in its own name to the approving office’s committee

beats.text: Just one came in the year after an approval. The calendar predicts about 0.2.

b: in the 365 days after an approval

beats.text: It happened once before, in 2014, after an amendment to the same lease.
297 days later, at Mayor Edwin Lee’s request, Autodesk gave 50,000 dollars to a foundation.

visual.label: to San Francisco Travel Foundation (SFUSCM 2015), 16 March 2015

beats.text: The Mayor’s notice was signed 24 days after the approval date.
The form gives five business days.
That is typical: 65.2 percent of the Mayor’s notices since 2019 were filed late.

visual.label: of the Mayor’s 3,830 notices since 2019 filed late (2,497)

beats.text: Here, that hid nothing.

visual.line: The contribution came long after this notice was on file, so the lateness hid nothing here.

beats.text: Not shown: whether a Port lease is covered, or whether the Mayor’s signature counts as the decision.

cards: Whether a Port lease is a covered contract
Whether the Mayor’s signature is a covered decision

beats.text: The request was disclosed, on the form the City provides for it.

beats.text: What would settle it? Any advice letter, waiver or complaint about this gift, and the signed lease.

beats.text: No one named here was contacted. No authority has made a finding.
A lead is a question, not an accusation.
